title: Mañana
goal: Talk about plans and make predictions with the future tense, and say what will happen if...

lessons.title: I will speak
lessons.notes:
The future tense is one of the easiest: keep the **whole infinitive** and add the endings (the same for -ar, -er and -ir):
**yo** hablaré · **tú** hablarás · **él / ella / usted** hablará · **nosotros** hablaremos · **ellos / ustedes** hablarán
**comeré**, **viviré**, **iré** (from ir), **seré**, **estaré**.
All but the **nosotros** form have an accent.
You already know **ir a** + infinitive for plans (**voy a viajar**). In everyday speech that's more common; the future (**viajaré**) sounds a little more certain or formal, and it's the natural choice for predictions and promises.

sentences.en: Tomorrow I'll speak with my boss.
accept_en: I'll talk to my boss tomorrow.
Tomorrow I will speak to my boss.

sentences.en: Will you talk to her tonight?
accept_en: Will you speak with her tonight?

sentences.es: Mi hija viajará a Chile el próximo año.
sentences.en: My daughter will travel to Chile next year.
accept_en: Next year my daughter will travel to Chile.
My daughter will go to Chile next year.

sentences.es: Un día viviremos en la playa.
sentences.en: One day we'll live by the beach.
accept_en: Someday we will live at the beach.
One day we'll live at the beach.

sentences.es: Mis padres estarán aquí la semana que viene.
sentences.en: My parents will be here next week.
The day after tomorrow I'll go to the doctor.
accept_en: I'll go to the doctor the day after tomorrow.
The day after tomorrow I'll see the doctor.

sentences.en: I promise you I'll be on time.
accept_en: I promise I'll be on time.
I promise you that I will be punctual.

sentences.en: What will you eat tomorrow?
The concert will be on Saturday.

lessons.title: Irregular futures
lessons.notes:
A dozen verbs use a shortened stem, but the endings stay the same (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án):
**tener -> tendr-**: tendré · **poner -> pondr-** · **salir -> saldr-** · **venir -> vendr-**
**poder -> podr-**: podré · **saber -> sabr-** · **querer -> querr-** · **haber -> habr-**
**hacer -> har-**: haré · **decir -> dir-**: diré
**habrá** = there will be (the future of **hay**).
Tip: these are the same verbs that were irregular in the preterite, so they'll start to look familiar.

sentences.es: El próximo año tendré más tiempo.
sentences.en: Next year I'll have more time.
accept_en: I'll have more time next year.
Next year I will have more time.

sentences.es: Mañana haré la tarea, te lo prometo.
sentences.en: I'll do the homework tomorrow, I promise.
accept_en: Tomorrow I'll do the homework, I promise you.
I'll do my homework tomorrow, I promise.

sentences.es: No podré ir a tu fiesta.
sentences.en: I won't be able to go to your party.
accept_en: I won't be able to come to your party.
I can't go to your party.

sentences.es: Saldremos a las seis de la mañana.
sentences.en: We'll leave at six in the morning.
accept_en: We will leave at six in the morning.
We'll set off at six in the morning.

sentences.en: My cousins will come in December.
accept_en: My cousins are coming in December.

sentences.en: What will your mum say?
accept_en: What's your mum going to say?

sentences.en: Tomorrow you'll know the truth.
accept_en: Tomorrow you'll find out the truth.

sentences.en: Will there be a lot of people at the beach?
accept_en: Will there be many people at the beach?

sentences.es: Pondré el abrigo en la maleta.
sentences.en: I'll put the coat in the suitcase.
accept_en: I will put the coat in the suitcase.
I'll pack the coat in the suitcase.

lessons.title: Predictions
lessons.notes:
The future is perfect for **predictions**. Soften them with:
**creo que** (I think that) · **seguro que** (surely, I bet) · **quizás / tal vez** (perhaps) · **probablemente** (probably)
**Creo que lloverá mañana.** = I think it'll rain tomorrow.
**Seguro que ganará el partido.** = I'm sure he'll win the game.
The future can also guess about the **present**: **¿Dónde estará Luis?** = I wonder where Luis is. **Estará en casa.** = He's probably at home.
Weather futures: **lloverá**, **hará calor**, **hará sol**.

sentences.en: I think it'll rain tomorrow.
accept_en: I think it will rain tomorrow.

sentences.es: Seguro que tu equipo ganará el partido.
sentences.en: I'm sure your team will win the match.
accept_en: Your team will surely win the game.
I bet your team will win the match.

sentences.es: Quizás iremos a la playa el domingo.
sentences.en: Perhaps we'll go to the beach on Sunday.
accept_en: Maybe we'll go to the beach on Sunday.

sentences.en: I'll probably arrive late.

sentences.es: En el futuro todo será diferente.
sentences.en: In the future everything will be different.
The city will change a lot.
I wonder where Luis is. - He's probably at home.
accept_en: Where can Luis be? - He must be at home.
Where could Luis be? - He'll be at home.

sentences.es: Creo que mañana hará mucho calor.
sentences.en: I think it'll be very hot tomorrow.
accept_en: I think tomorrow will be very hot.
I think it will be really hot tomorrow.

lessons.title: If it rains...
lessons.notes:
For real possibilities: **si** + **present**, then the **future** (or ir a, or the present):
**Si llueve, me quedaré en casa.** = If it rains, I'll stay at home.
**Si tengo tiempo, te llamo.** = If I have time, I'll call you.
Just like English, the **si** part never uses the future: not "si lloverá".
You can swap the halves: **Te llamo si tengo tiempo.** (no comma then).
Careful with the accent: **si** = if; **sí** = yes.
**cuando** for the future works differently - you'll meet it at B1. For now, use **si**.

sentences.es: Si llueve, me quedaré en casa.
sentences.en: If it rains, I'll stay at home.
accept_en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
If it rains I will stay at home.

sentences.en: If I have time, I'll call you.
accept_en: If I have time, I'll ring you.
If I've got time, I'll call you.

sentences.en: I'll help you if I can.
If you win the lottery, what will you do?

sentences.es: Si ahorro dinero, viajaré a España.
sentences.en: If I save money, I'll travel to Spain.
accept_en: If I save money, I'll go to Spain.
If I save money I will travel to Spain.

sentences.es: Si no te sientes bien, llama al médico.
sentences.en: If you don't feel well, call the doctor.
accept_en: If you're not feeling well, call the doctor.

sentences.es: Si hace sol, iremos a la playa.
sentences.en: If it's sunny, we'll go to the beach.
accept_en: If it is sunny, we will go to the beach.

sentences.es: Si sales tarde, perderás el autobús.
sentences.en: If you leave late, you'll miss the bus.
accept_en: If you leave late, you will miss the bus.

sentences.en: If you want, I'll call you tomorrow.
accept_en: If you like, I'll call you tomorrow.
I'll ring you tomorrow if you want.
